notes: Context: mid-market B2B SaaS — in-app assistant + support agent to reduce CS load and improve activation
Initial approach: started on Redwood hosted_api for quick proof-of-value (Jan demo). Low-friction integration via SDK worked well.
POC summary: 6-week POC (hosted) validating prompt templates, latency, and cost model. Key metric: reduce average support handle time by 22% (target 20%).
Traffic profile: peak concurrency ~45 req/s, avg tokens per response 120, expected steady-state tokens/mo ~180M with seasonal spikes to 300M.
Latency SLOs: 95th perc < 350ms for typical chat flows; critical for embedded UI. Careful about cold-starts and KV cache behavior.
Security notes: must support SSO/SAML, tenant-level audit logs, and option to store logs in customer-owned S3. Data residency: EU for subset of accounts.
Initial ask to Redwood: pricing for Dedicated with monthly commits, burst capacity for seasonal spikes, predictable overage rates, and a 3-month ramp schedule.
AE notes from 2/18: 'liked the runtime telemetry — token breakdown per route is huge for finance justification.'
SE input (Daniel): recommended Dedicated with 2-tier model variants (quantized vs full precision) and prefix caching to hit latency/cost targets.
Finance feedback: wants a 12-month uplift discount if commit >= $80k/month; otherwise prefers quarterly commits. Wants explicit overage cap or blended rate.
Legal asks: add clause for returning or deleting cached user content after 30 days; clarify KMS integration and key ownership for Private later.
Competition: evaluating alternative reserved capacity with vendor X — price slightly lower but lacks token-level cost telemetry and rollout tooling.
Internal momentum: product execs favor Redwood for rollout speed; CTO wants private deployment option in 2027 for regulated customers.
POC results: hosted POC met accuracy and latency targets in 90% of test scenarios; exceptions around long-form summarization prompted model tuning.
Negotiation points outstanding: commit tiers (50M / 150M / 300M tokens), burst policy (3x baseline for 30 minutes), overage unit price, ramp credits for Q1-Kickoff.
Customer quote: 'We need a predictable monthly bill that scales with usage — spikes can't break our unit economics.'
Next commercial ask sent 3/2: draft SOW and a 12-month committed pricing sheet with ramp schedule + burst add-on options.
Follow-up: pricing call scheduled 3/9 to lock in final commit level; AE to circulate redlined pricing sheet beforehand.
